summary: Gone log cupola cabin, built in 1927 near Kellogg, Idaho; destroyed in 1955. Only names carved into rocks remain at the site.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1955. Idaho Fire Lookouts found almost nothing left, not even the cement footings.

staffing.status: named lookouts from 1939 to 1948 in the sources

access.note: On Coeur d'Alene National Forest land and listed as drive-up. The level is inferred from the forest and drive-up notes; no source states an access rule.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com spells the 1944 lookout Warner McGillvray. Idaho Fire Lookouts spells it Werner McGillvray. The story gives the Idaho spelling and notes the other.
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts put the 1931 patrol tower one mile west. Forest Lookouts puts it one mile northwest. The story reports both.
A 1928 inspection report, as quoted on Forest Lookouts, calls the building the Cougar Mountain Lookout. The story uses the Cougar Peak name the sources use for the site.

notes_for_editor: Three web pages and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The core dates (1927 build, 1955 destruction) agree across sources. Do not confuse this with the Montana Cougar Peak Lookout on the Lolo National Forest, a different structure that is standing, rentable, and has its own record (us-mt-cougar-peak). A search result from the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Facebook page and a Flickr photo caption for a 1952 rentable Cougar Peak Lookout describe the Montana building; they were not used here. The 1928 inspection report and the 1962 Kellogg Evening News item are quoted second-hand; the originals were not fetched. The Kellogg Evening News is the source for the first lookout, Bus Peterson. The brief's ground kind matches the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The access level public is inferred from forest land and the drive-up label. Staffing names are given as the sources list them; no source covers staffing after 1948.
